text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
NASA BORBA

- European Union Council of Ministers to discuss restoring Yugoslavia's trade preferentials, abolished in November 1991, in Luxembourg on Tuesday. Ethnic Albanian leader calls on EU not to grant Belgrade trade concessions until Kosovo issue resolved.

- International mediator for questions of succession of former Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts offers ex-Yugoslav republics three new proposals on division of the former federation's assets. No reports in local media on Watts' visit to Belgrade last Thursday.
- Coordination committee of Kosovo Albanian political parties could decide Tuesday on holding Albanian elections in Serbia's majority Albanian province.

- "War" in Montenegrin ruling party leadership continues. Republican President Momir Bulatovic dissatisfied with results of efforts so far to force Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic to carry out his orders, Montena-Fax news agency said.
- Large hard currency debtors and banks with dinar investments fear dinar's devaluation, while huge dinar debtors and exporters would welcome it.

- Merryll Lynch presents two scenarios for Yugoslavia's agreement with foreign creditors. Price of Yugoslav foreign debt determined by length of political crisis. Current indebtedness estimated to be 70 percent of GDP.

- "So far, I am certain no part of PTT system has been sold to anyone," says PTT trade union secretary Marjan Djukic. Some 30,000 PTT employees interested in the fate of Serbia's postal company and its status in forthcoming ownership transformation.
- Kosovo Albanian Emigration Commission president Rifat Bljaku says return of Albanians from Germany being speeded up.
- In the first three months of the year, 16,500 cases of infectious diseases registered in Kosovo, 25 deaths from various diseases.
- Catholic Archbishop of Belgrade France Perko says the Pope could visit Belgrade next year "if circumstances permit".
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce president Mihailo Milojevic meets Airbus representatives. Airbus sales director Otmar Krinner says his company is prepared to assist Yugoslav airlines JAT in reconstruction of its fleet.
- Twenty Slovenian firms to attend agricultural fair in Novi Sad. Slovenian businessmen say firms should "go ahead of politics and cooperate more".
- Yugoslav exports last year 2.2 times below the level in 1987, raw materials dominate in structure of exports.

- If the state has already given income from smuggled cigarettes which account for 90 percent of total sales, why not do the same for the remaining 10 percent and so enable the country's tobacco industry to survive?
- UNHCR granted around 2,000 credits to refugees in Yugoslavia for private businesses as part of process of securing economic independence for refugees.
- Registration of voters for local elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina from May 5 to June 16.
- Japanese government approves $10 million as support to UNHCR for revival programmes for priority regions in Bosnia-Herzegovina.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- U.S. Ambassador to Croatia warns rehabilitation of World War Two Croatian fascist leader Ante Pavelic unacceptable.
- Croatian Defence Minister Gojko Susak announces signing of agreement with Yugoslavia soon on demilitarisation of Eastern Slavonia region.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT and Bulgaria's Balkan Air agree on regular Belgrade-Sofia flights three times a week from May 26.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Pro-Monte, GSM Mobile telephone company, on Monday started operating in northern Montenegrin municipalities of Bijelo Polje, Berane and Kolasin.
- Hotel Avala in Budva has sold out its capacities to Israeli tourists until the end of summer season.
- There are some 32,235 workers employed in Montenegrin industry, compared to 55,945 six years ago.
- Three Montenegrin state funds -- Development Fund, Pensioners Fun and Fund for Unemployed -- to privatise 40 small and medium companies this and next week.
- UNESCO expert mission visited Biogradska Gora national park near Kolasin to ascertain if the park meets UNESCO criteria for the world natural heritage list. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
